name: Glacier de Corbassière

summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2016, 2023), swisstopo lidar (27 tiles of 2021) and the GLAMOS annual balance of Glacier de Corbassière per elevation band for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025, all-combinations file) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2019" with date_end 20169999: survey 2016, day unknown. Image strips over the strip in 2016 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2016-08-25 TLM (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the model puts the whole edition on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2016-08-25 (a day a strip was flown, taken from the pair of flown days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (1.59 m); ties within 0.05 m go to the GLAMOS date if it is among them, else to the strip covering most ice. Chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 27 tiles read (tiles with ice). 19 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-09-22 on 9, 2021-09-24 on 6, 2021-10-10 on 4); 8 tiles were flown on several days within 60 days and take the point-weighted mean day (uncertain by up to about a month); 0 tiles flown on days further apart (or not read) are not used. The lidar sits on 100 % of the ice cells (computed).
anchors.placed_at: the flight day of each tile (see above)

anchors.survey: Built from aerial images 2023: strips over the ice 2023-09-07 SWISSIMAGE (100 % of ice cells, computed). GLAMOS names 20230823 (is-stand). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-09-07 (a day a strip was flown, chosen with A1 by the same pair rule)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of each elevation band, from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt even from 1 May: an assumption) to 30 September. The band balance is the GLAMOS annual balance of Glacier de Corbassière itself (release 2025, 100 m bins from 2300 m, which cover the whole tongue; non-commercial); it only decides how the change between two surveys is spread over the years and heights, the size comes from the surveys. 2026 is not in release 2025: its bands are ESTIMATED (computed here): each Glacier de Corbassière band regressed on the glacier-wide Bw and Bs of Grosser Aletsch (2005 to 2025) and evaluated at the Aletsch 2026 values read from the GLAMOS figure (Bw +751.6, Bs -3790.0 mm w.e., about +-100 mm w.e.). Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the rate of the last segment is applied to the measured 2023 surface, from the anchor difference smoothed over about 100 m (the raw difference carries noise and made 2024 to 2026 rough). The ground outside the 2023 outline stays at its 2023 height and no fade is applied, so a step grows along the outline (median lowering of the ice cells next to it 0.7 m in 2024, 1.3 m in 2025, 3.2 m in 2026, computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band at the nearest anchor.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007: 4,033 shots on 2023 ice in 18 granules (July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, inside the physical envelope). rmse 1.59 m over all years, bias +0.85 m (model minus shot), leave-one-granule-out: the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored; with the days used 1.59 m. Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2018 3.23 m (202 shots); 2019 1.71 m (342 shots); 2020 1.96 m (557 shots); 2021 1.39 m (337 shots); 2022 1.54 m (621 shots); 2023 1.34 m (1151 shots); 2024 0.68 m (491 shots); 2025 1.33 m (332 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 12588 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.47 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September); ICESat-2 scores years with shots, not each year step. 13 of 131 ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) passed the gate (rock NMAD at most 15 m, at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells) in 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2024; ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres mean something. GLAMOS stake readings (57 stake-years, annual files, type 1, on modelled ice inside the 2023 outline) are a check of the year-to-year split: the modelled surface change is 0.78 of the stake reading on average (RMSE 0.79 m), as expected because stakes move with the ice.

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne research DEMs and TanDEM-X series: the RAGMAC set covers Aletsch only (read); a first search for others is recorded in the source ledger of this glacier, and none was used; no radar surface was used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). The GLAMOS balances of Glacier de Corbassière and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

page.areaTitle: the 3D strip of Glacier de Corbassière

bed.lead: Three checks on Glacier de Corbassière (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 1,885 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −0.7 m over all cells, but it depends on the survey: −0.6 m (2011, 1,621 cells), −7.9 m (1998, 190 cells), +5.1 m (1988, 74 cells). Spread (standard deviation) 6.7 m in 2011, 17.3 m in 1998, 8.7 m in 1988; over all cells 85 % are within 10 m and 99 % within 30 m.

Reading: the 2011 survey agrees closest (90 % of its cells within 10 m) and the 1998 survey least (45 %). This is not a validation: the model bed was made from these same surveys (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Only 76 spots (25 m cells) have two survey dates (1998 and 2011: 26, 1988 and 2011: 50). The beds implied by the two surveys differ by a median −6.0 m (later minus earlier) with a standard deviation of 20.3 m; 59 % agree within 10 m.

Reading: enough spots for a rough measure of how the surveys repeat.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

279 points (278 from 2011, 1 from 1988) on 2 flight profiles, ice about 56 m thick:

2011
Radar bed − ground now+10.1 m (−2.8 to +19.9)
Model bed − ground now+7.1 m (−1.2 to +16.1)

Median, in brackets the middle half (years with too few points are not shown). 72 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

bed.key: Each dot is one radar point of the survey years on the strip, in ground that is ice free in the newest swissALTI3D. Light blue: ice in the SGI2023 outline; dashed: the SGI2016 outline, the ice the model was made for. The points lie in the strip between the two outlines, kept 30 m clear of both. They come from 2 flight profiles.
bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins the radar bed lies 10.0 m above the exposed ground and the model bed 7.0 m above it (medians of the points of 2011).

What it does not show

  • Few places: the 279 points lie on 2 flight profiles, at the margins where the ice is about 56 m thick; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • No error band: the GLAMOS release has no uncertainty maps for the model bed, and swissBEDROCK's band under glaciers is about 0. Lakes, debris and the margin position (a few metres) were not screened.

How the points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline and 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there; newest swissALTI3D, slope at most 20°. With up to 30°: 496 points; with a 50 m margin: 110 points; with 100 m: none.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 1.34 m (rmse of the 1151 shots of 2023). The lidar of 2021 carries 1.34 m (the same as the surveys, because fewer than 30 shots lie within 45 days of the lidar day). swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above (as quoted by Bannwart et al.), so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high. Between and beyond the surveys the error grows with the size of the change (factors 0.35 and 0.00), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent; where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 1.5 m).
notes.sharing: Solid: the GLAMOS annual balance of Glacier de Corbassière per elevation band sets how the loss between two surveys falls into each year. Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (13 of 131 scenes usable; usable years: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2024). GLAMOS stakes (57 stake-years on modelled ice) are checks only. Click a year for the numbers.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. About 7 MB, loaded when you press the button.
page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 14.1 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2016 survey, about 15.3 km² (computed). The 4,033 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). Every modelled ice cell lies within 1 km of an ICESat-2 shot used for the check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.stakeNote: Over all 57 stake-years the modelled surface change is 0.78 of the stake reading (RMSE 0.79 m). Stakes read ablation of moving ice, so the model is expected to show a fraction. By year the ratio is 2017 0.79, 2018 0.81, 2019 0.76, 2020 0.72, 2021 0.85, 2022 0.80, 2023 0.82, 2024 0.68, 2025 0.78 (computed). Check only, not in the fit.
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 9.7 to 14.7 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
